FINAL OWNER DIRECTIVE — COMPLETE IVX INDEPENDENCE

My decision is final:

I want IVX to operate with:

- My own code
- My own GitHub repositories
- My own dependencies
- My own AI provider accounts
- My own autonomous AI developer
- My own deployment pipeline
- My own infrastructure
- My own credentials
- My own build and release process

TARGET

RORK ACTIVE DEPENDENCY = 0%

Rork may assist with this migration, but IVX must continue operating after all Rork access is removed.

Do not preserve Rork platform dependencies for convenience.

==================================================
1. CODE OWNERSHIP
==================================================

Verify that all active IVX production code exists in an owner-controlled repository.

Required repository owner:

ibb142

Audit all active repositories and branches.

Return:

- Repository
- Owner
- Default branch
- Production branch
- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Render-linked repository
- Mobile build repository
- Worker repository
- Any submodules
- Any external Git dependencies
- Rork-owned repository dependency: YES / NO

Requirements:

- Preserve full Git history.
- Preserve branches and tags.
- No active code may exist only inside the Rork sandbox.
- Export and commit every required source file.
- No production build may depend on unpublished sandbox files.

==================================================
2. CREATE AN IVX-NAMED PRIMARY REPOSITORY
==================================================

Create or migrate to an owner-controlled repository with an IVX name, such as:

ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform

Requirements:

1. Preserve complete Git history.
2. Push all required branches and tags.
3. Verify commit parity with the current production repository.
4. Update Render to use the new IVX repository.
5. Update CI/CD.
6. Update documentation and deployment scripts.
7. Verify production before archiving the old repository.

Do not delete or archive the current repository until the new repository is live and verified.

The old repository name containing “rork” must not remain the permanent production source.

==================================================
3. REMOVE RORK SOURCE AND CONFIG DEPENDENCIES
==================================================

Audit and remove all active:

- Rork imports
- Rork SDKs
- Rork packages
- Rork API clients
- Rork proxy clients
- Rork build plugins
- Rork runtime hooks
- Rork telemetry
- Rork authentication
- Rork environment variables
- Rork URLs
- Rork webhooks
- Rork update services
- Rork private registries

Search:

rork
rork.com
rork.app
rork.dev
rork-sdk
rork_api
RORK_API_KEY
RORK_TOKEN
RORK_SECRET
RORK_PROJECT_ID
EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_
rork.json

For every finding return:

- File
- Line
- Active / inactive / legacy
- Purpose
- Replacement
- Removal status
- Verification

Remove active dependencies only after the replacement passes.

==================================================
4. OWN DEPENDENCIES
==================================================

Create a complete software bill of materials.

Audit:

- package.json
- lockfiles
- Podfile
- Gradle
- Expo plugins
- Native modules
- Docker images
- GitHub Actions
- Build scripts

For every dependency return:

- Package
- Version
- Publisher
- Registry
- Direct / transitive
- Purpose
- License
- Maintained status
- Security status
- Rork-owned: YES / NO
- Approved for IVX: YES / NO

Requirements:

- No Rork-owned package.
- No Rork private registry.
- No dependency downloaded from a Rork domain.
- Use public or IVX-controlled dependencies.
- Pin production versions.
- Regenerate lockfiles.
- Add dependency vulnerability scanning.

==================================================
5. OWN AI PROVIDER
==================================================

Replace every Rork AI gateway or proxy with direct IVX-controlled provider access.

Approved architecture:

IVX APPLICATION
→ IVX BACKEND
→ APPROVED AI PROVIDER

No Rork proxy between IVX and the AI provider.

Audit all AI use cases:

- IVX IA chat
- Senior developer AI
- Public chat
- Autonomous planning
- Document analysis
- Image analysis
- Video analysis
- Marketing AI
- Investor assistant
- Reports

For each return:

- Source file
- Current provider
- Current base URL
- Current key variable
- Direct or proxy
- New provider
- New IVX-owned variable
- Migration status

Use IVX-controlled credentials such as:

OPENAI_API_KEY
or another owner-approved provider key.

Never expose the key in mobile or frontend code.

Only the backend or secure worker may read it.

==================================================
6. OWN AI DEVELOPER
==================================================

Build the IVX Senior Developer as an IVX-controlled service.

Service name:

ivx-senior-dev-01

It must not depend on Rork chat or Rork runtime.

Capabilities:

- Read the IVX repository
- Create branches
- Edit code
- Run tests
- Run type checks
- Run security checks
- Build website
- Build API
- Build worker
- Build Android
- Prepare iOS build
- Create commits
- Push approved changes
- Trigger deployments
- Verify health
- Verify version parity
- Run QA jobs
- Pause/resume/cancel jobs
- Retry failed jobs
- Write proof ledger records
- Produce owner reports

Security:

- Owner approval before production mutation
- Exact commit binding
- Short-lived single-use authorization
- Worker HMAC identity
- Replay rejection
- Audit logs
- No permanent owner session token
- No production secret in logs

==================================================
7. OWN AUTONOMOUS CONTROL PLANE
==================================================

The control plane must operate through IVX services only.

Required flow:

OWNER LOGIN
→ IVX OWNER DASHBOARD
→ OWNER APPROVAL
→ IVX WORKER AUTHORIZATION
→ IVX SENIOR DEVELOPER
→ GITHUB
→ BUILD
→ RENDER
→ HEALTH CHECK
→ PROOF LEDGER

Rork must not be in this runtime chain.

Required controls:

- Queue
- Approve
- Start
- Pause
- Resume
- Cancel
- Retry
- Block
- Recover stale task
- Dead-letter
- Replay rejection
- Rollback

==================================================
8. OWN BUILD PIPELINE
==================================================

Replace Rork CI/build convenience with IVX-controlled build infrastructure.

Use one or more owner-controlled systems:

- GitHub Actions
- Render native deploys
- Expo/EAS under the owner's account
- IVX-controlled build worker

Create pipelines for:

A. Website
B. API
C. Autonomous worker
D. Android APK
E. iOS build

Each pipeline must include:

- Checkout
- Dependency install
- Lint
- Type check
- Unit tests
- Integration tests
- Security scan
- Build
- Artifact creation
- Deployment
- Health check
- Version check
- Rollback point

No workflow may require a Rork account or Rork session.

==================================================
9. OWN DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

Production deployment must be controlled by IVX accounts.

Audit and verify:

- Render workspace owner
- Render API service
- Render worker service
- Environment groups
- Deploy hooks
- GitHub integration
- Custom domains
- Health checks
- Rollback
- Auto-deploy rules

Requirements:

- No Rork workspace dependency.
- No Rork-owned deploy hook.
- No Rork bot required.
- No Rork proxy in front of the API.
- No Rork build image.

==================================================
10. OWN EXPO AND MOBILE BUILDS
==================================================

Verify Expo/EAS ownership.

Return:

- Expo account owner
- Project ID
- Android application ID
- iOS bundle ID
- Update URL
- Runtime version
- Signing ownership
- Build profiles

Requirements:

- No Rork Expo project.
- No Rork EAS owner.
- No Rork OTA endpoint.
- No Rork signing identity.
- Android and iOS build without Rork.

No App Store or Google Play submission is required now.

==================================================
11. OWN AUTHENTICATION
==================================================

User and owner authentication must use an IVX-approved provider directly.

Current expected provider:

Supabase Auth

Verify:

- Supabase organization ownership
- Project ownership
- Owner user record
- Redirect URLs
- JWT validation
- Session refresh
- RLS
- Service-role isolation
- Worker authorization

Requirements:

- No Rork-issued identity.
- No Rork token validator.
- No owner token copied through Rork chat.
- Owner approval occurs inside IVX.

==================================================
12. OWN DATABASE AND STORAGE
==================================================

Verify IVX control of:

- Supabase database
- Supabase storage
- Realtime
- Backups
- Migrations
- Edge Functions
- Webhooks
- RLS policies

Requirements:

- No Rork database.
- No Rork storage bucket.
- No Rork webhook.
- No Rork redirect URL.
- No Rork-controlled service account.

==================================================
13. OWN DOMAINS AND NETWORK
==================================================

Verify all production domains:

- ivxholding.com
- www.ivxholding.com
- api.ivxholding.com
- chat.ivxholding.com

Audit:

- DNS
- SSL
- CDN
- API origins
- WebSockets
- Upload hosts
- Asset hosts
- Redirects

Required result:

Rork-owned production hostnames contacted = 0

No Rork:

- domain
- redirect
- cookie
- WebSocket
- asset URL
- telemetry endpoint
- background request

==================================================
14. OWN MONITORING
==================================================

Implement IVX-controlled monitoring for:

- Website uptime
- API uptime
- Worker heartbeat
- Owner login failures
- HTTP 500 errors
- Queue backlog
- Failed deployments
- Dead-letter jobs
- Chat failures
- Reels crashes
- CPU
- Memory
- Database health

No monitoring data may be sent to Rork.

==================================================
15. CLEAN-ROOM BUILD
==================================================

Run a clean-room verification outside Rork.

Conditions:

- Fresh checkout
- No Rork login
- No Rork session
- No Rork API key
- No Rork SDK
- No Rork environment variable
- No cached Rork package
- No Rork build service

Execute:

1. Install dependencies.
2. Run lint.
3. Run type checks.
4. Run tests.
5. Build website.
6. Build API.
7. Build worker.
8. Build Android APK.
9. Prepare iOS build.
10. Start API.
11. Start worker.
12. Call /health.
13. Call /version.
14. Run one owner-approved QA job.

This clean-room build must run from IVX-controlled infrastructure.

==================================================
16. CUTOVER PLAN
==================================================

Perform migration in this order:

1. Freeze current production.
2. Record rollback SHA.
3. Create IVX-named repository.
4. Mirror full history.
5. Replace Rork AI gateway.
6. Replace Rork build pipeline.
7. Deploy IVX API.
8. Deploy IVX worker.
9. Deploy website.
10. Build Android.
11. Verify iOS build.
12. Run network scan.
13. Run autonomous QA.
14. Remove orphaned Rork variables.
15. Remove rork.json.
16. Disable Rork deploy hooks.
17. Verify no Rork access is required.
18. Freeze independent release.

Do not sever the old path until the replacement passes.

==================================================
17. FINAL PROOF
==================================================

Return:

CODE OWNERSHIP
- Primary IVX repository:
- Repository owner:
- GitHub HEAD:
- Full history preserved:
- Rork-only source files remaining:

DEPENDENCIES
- Active Rork packages:
- Active Rork SDKs:
- Active Rork registries:
- Active Rork environment variables:

AI
- AI provider:
- Direct IVX provider call:
- Rork gateway used:
- IVX worker AI key loaded:

BUILD
- GitHub Actions:
- Render deploy:
- Android build:
- iOS build:
- Rork CI required:

RUNTIME
- Rork domains contacted:
- Rork APIs called:
- Rork WebSockets:
- Rork telemetry:
- Rork authentication:

AUTONOMOUS DEVELOPER
- Worker service:
- Worker service ID:
- Worker live SHA:
- Owner approval:
- Job ID:
- Proof ledger ID:
- Replay rejection:

PRODUCTION
- Website HTTP status:
- API /health:
- API /version:
- Public chat:
- Owner login:
- Worker heartbeat:
- GitHub SHA = live SHA:

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE
==================================================

Mark IVX FULLY INDEPENDENT = PASS only when:

- Code is in an IVX-named owner-controlled repository.
- No production source exists only in Rork.
- No Rork API remains.
- No Rork SDK remains.
- No Rork package remains.
- No Rork environment variable remains active.
- No Rork AI gateway remains.
- No Rork CI/build pipeline is required.
- No Rork deployment service is required.
- No Rork authentication remains.
- No Rork runtime traffic exists.
- No Rork telemetry exists.
- Website builds without Rork.
- API builds and deploys without Rork.
- Worker runs without Rork.
- Android builds without Rork.
- iOS build is independent from Rork.
- Owner approval occurs inside IVX.
- IVX Senior Developer completes a QA job without Rork.
- Clean-room build passes.
- Production continues operating after Rork access is removed.

FINAL STATUS:

IVX CODE OWNERSHIP:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

IVX DEPENDENCY OWNERSHIP:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

IVX AI DEVELOPER INDEPENDENCE:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

RORK ACTIVE DEPENDENCY:
0% / NOT YET 0%

Do not return another high-level plan.

Execute the migration in controlled phases and return evidence after every phase.
